correctness.rationale: Domination in KG(n,2) is equivalent to each unselected two-element pair failing to cover selected edges; hence every 2-cover must itself be a selected edge. For an inclusion-minimal dominating family H, tau(H)=1 forces full star; tau=2, taking selected cover ab and excluding triangles, forces at least two disjoint leaves at each side, hence 5-edge balanced double star. For tau>=3, any triangle or matching of size three gives a smaller dominating family, so otherwise no triangle and matching number <=2: by Konig a bipartite graph would have tau<=2, and shortest odd cycle is necessarily C5. Deletion witnesses show exactly all five families are minimal; orbit counts give displayed polynomial. Independent exhaustive n=5,6 calculations found 27 and 203, agreeing with formula; these are bounded crosschecks, not infinite proof.
